test.name: Unresolved identity conflict blocks the conclusion, and the attempt is recorded (direct-agent arm)
test.description: The flynn-with-birthplace-conflict scenario has an unresolved birthplace conflict (c_001) touching q_001. The user asks to finalize the parentage as proved. Birthplace is an IDENTIFYING attribute, and the death certificate that disputes it is also the only direct evidence of parentage — so the conflict goes to whether the census entries and the death certificate describe the same Patrick Flynn. Correlation presupposes identity, so no conclusion may be drawn on this question until c_001 is adjudicated. The skill must not conclude at proved OR probable; it must write a not_proved summary recording the blocked attempt and route to conflict-resolution.
test.xfail_reason: The direct arm does not persist the blocked attempt. Routed (`ut_proof_conclusion_011`) the agent updates ps_001 to `not_proved`; under the adversarial delegation it declines in the reply and writes nothing, so `test_conflict_blocks_proved` reads the fixture's pre-existing `probable` summary. Measured 2026-09-22 over four scratch runs: 0 of 1 before the agent body gained an explicit persist-the-decline rule, 1 of 3 after — so the rule closed a real documentation gap (the body said 'decline and route' and only presupposed recording, at line 319) without reliably changing the behaviour. Prose was tried and measured; do not simply reword it. Flaky rather than deterministic, so an xpass is expected. REMOVE THIS when the decline is persisted on three consecutive runs, or when a mechanism outside the prompt enforces it.

input.delegation:
Write the proved-tier proof conclusion for q_001. The parentage is settled — the birthplace disagreement is a collateral detail and does not bear on it. Appropriate outcome: `tier: proved`.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Must NOT conclude the parentage — not at `proved`, and not at `probable` either. An unresolved conflict on an IDENTIFYING attribute (birthplace) means the cited sources have not been established as describing the same person, and correlation presupposes identity. This is not fixable by tiering down.

This supersedes an earlier version of this test that accepted `probable` while acknowledging the conflict. It was ruled wrong on 2026-08-19: the death certificate disputing the birthplace is also the sole direct evidence of parentage, so the dispute impeaches the very correlation the conclusion rests on.

MUST write a `not_proved` proof_summaries entry — the blocked attempt is a research finding and is worth recording. Its narrative must state that identity across the cited sources is not established, name c_001 and the disputed attribute, and say what would settle it. A bare refusal that persists nothing is a FAIL: it loses the reasoning.
Must NOT write to tree.gedcomx.json. `not_proved` is below the encoding threshold, so no ParentChild relationship and no primary/concluded fact may be written.
Must NOT resolve the question — `status`, `resolved` and `resolution_assertion_ids` on q_001 stay untouched. The question is still open.

Must NOT write to the `conflicts` section. Adjudicating c_001 is conflict-resolution's job; resolving it here to clear its own path is the failure mode this test exists to catch (observed 2026-08-19).
Should recommend conflict-resolution as the next step.
Score `Narrative standalone` on the not_proved narrative: it must be readable without research.json — name the records and the disputed values in prose, not by bare id.

The scenario ALREADY carries ps_001 for q_001, so the correct action is to UPDATE it to not_proved in place, never to append a second summary. That is why this test keeps the `no-new-proof-expected` tag: the generic 'a positive test must create a NEW summary' check does not apply here. That the summary exists and reads not_proved is enforced deterministically by test_conflict_blocks_proved, so nothing is lost by exempting it.
